t: Jim Keller: Moore's Law, Microprocessors, and First Principles | Lex Fridman Podcast #70

q.x: If you haven't already, highly suggest watching his Lex Fridman interview. I learned a lot from it, both about chips and Keller. [link]

desc:
Jim Keller is a legendary microprocessor engineer, having worked at AMD, Apple, Tesla, and now Intel. He's known for his work on the AMD K7, K8, K12 and Zen microarchitectures, Apple A4, A5 processors, and co-author of the specifications for the x86-64 instruction set and HyperTransport interconnect.

This episode is presented by Cash App. Download it & use code "LexPodcast":

recs.stt: How much better was DEC Alpha than contemporary x86?
recs.x: I highly suggest viewing one of the Alpha's original designers, Jim Keller, recent chat with MIT Prof Lex Fridman [link] I was stunned by Jim's total command of Computer Architecture, and his deep insights about the subject. I will never again utter the phrase 'modern computer' without requisite awe.
